_comment: Model bank for the ported gen_random_workload.py, platform qrb5165_flowc.
One entry per Flow C binding manifest. dispatch_deps_path points at the
COARSE dispatch graph flowc/artifacts.py emits (one dispatch per tile),
because that is the dispatch space the schedule is solved in and the one
the emitted runtime can actually execute: mlp_control 1 tile, dronet 1,
fused_split 3, yolov8n 2, vint 2.
Matched arms: `dronet` and `fused_split` carry IDENTICAL period_ms,
window_ms and count bands and sit in the same position of the bank's
order, so --include-models mlp_control,dronet,yolov8n and
--include-models mlp_control,fused_split,yolov8n consume the same RNG
draws in the same order. Only the model in the mid-size periodic slot
differs -- which is the comparison the sweep is for.
Period bands are DECLARED rates, not multiples of measured runtime, the
same convention the FPGA bank uses. They are set from what Flow C's own
shipped workloads run these networks at on this board
(qnn_models/flow_c/workloads/*.json): mlp_control at 2 ms (500 Hz
control policy), the mid-size perception net at 5-20 ms. The FPGA bank's
5-20 / 20-100 ms bands are NOT reused: this board is 20-40x faster on
these networks, and a 100 ms period here is a nearly idle lane.
yolov8n keeps the FPGA bank's count {0,5} band on purpose, including the
zero: a seed that draws no detection has no non-periodic work and is
REJECTED by predicate 4, exactly as on the FPGA (4 of 16 points there).
vint takes count {1,2} rather than the FPGA's {0,2}, because Sweep B is
only 2 points and its entire question is what a heavy vision model does
to the schedule -- a seed that drew zero ViNT would answer nothing. That
is the one deliberate deviation from the FPGA bank's draw shape and it
affects only the fused_vint arm.

mlp_control.variant_note: Control policy, 1 tile. CPU cell is the fp32 context (107.3 us): QnnCpu's int8 path returns a constant for this network regardless of input (measurements/qrb5165_v66.json, _correctness_note in bindings/mlp_control.json). HTA is capability-excluded (elu_s8), so its profile row carries the derived exclusion cost.

dronet.variant_note: Steering CNN, 1 tile, composes on all three lanes (hta 2.03 ms / dsp 0.645 / cpu 7.00). The baseline arm's mid-size periodic slot.

fused_split.variant_note: FusedSensorNet cut into its two parallel conv branches plus the LSTM tail (3 tiles). This is the `fused_full` of SETUP.md's arm table -- SETUP.md's cell list for that arm is vision_conv/depth_conv/tail, which are fused_split's tiles, not the monolith's single fused_full_net cell. The split is also the only version with HTA coverage, so it is the one that exercises the third lane.

yolov8n.variant_note: 640x640 ultralytics export, backbone + head (2 tiles), ~28.6 ms serial on the DSP. The head is capability-excluded on HTA (Transpose), so its HTA profile row carries the derived exclusion cost. NOT the FPGA bank's 64x64 yolov8_nano -- no cross-target latency comparison is valid.

vint.variant_note: ViNT visual-nav transformer, encoders + decoder (2 tiles). The encoders run on the DSP (14.2 ms) and the decoder only on the CPU. Its CPU cell is load-dependent by construction -- see the confounds section of SETUP.md.
